The `tf.SparseTensor` requires indices as a dense tensor of shape `[num_elems, ndims]`, but the code passes `idx` (shape `[N, 2]`) without ensuring proper dimensions. Additionally, PyTorch's `torch.sparse_coo_tensor` expects indices in COO format (shape `[ndims, num_elems]`), but `.T` transposes to `[2, N]` which is incorrect for non-2D tensors. This mismatch will cause runtime errors during sparse mode tests.
